At a Glance

Are you an in-service music educator who wants practical, music-specific professional development? TCNJ’s graduate certificate in conducting (instrumental and choral tracks) pairs educators with TCNJ’s world-class conducting faculty for a unique, highly personalized program. Refine your physical gesture, develop your rehearsal technique, explore score study, and advance your conducting career. The program includes a capstone conducting recital, with the option for it to be completed with a TCNJ large ensemble or your own school ensemble.

Program Coordinator: Eric Laprade, lapradee@tcnj.edu

Who Should Pursue This Program?

With a flexible 12–15 credit curriculum, TCNJ’s unique graduate certificate in conducting is designed to meet your goals and is available to educators with an earned bachelor’s or master’s degree:

  • Already have a graduate degree? Earn 15 credits of music-specific training and move up the pay scale.
  • Earn a 30-credit master’s degree at TCNJ by stacking the conducting certificate with another one of TCNJ’s graduate certificates.
  • Prepare for and become more competitive for professional and graduate conducting degree auditions.

Curriculum

Required (12 credits):

  • MUSC 527: Conducting Lessons (3 semesters)
  • MUSC 697: Independent Study / Recital

Optional (3 credits):

  • MUSC 658: Social Justice, Music, Education

Application Requirements

For your application to be considered complete, you must submit the online application as well as all supplemental documents.

  • An official transcript from each college you have attended other than TCNJ is required.
  • References from two individuals who can evaluate your academic performance, relevant work experience, and/or ability to pursue graduate study.
  • Resume/CV (with a bulleted list of activities with participation dates).
  • Links to recent (last 5 years) conducting and rehearsal footage, in which the conductor is facing the camera. Video submissions should include: Ca. 5-10 minutes of rehearsal footage and ca. Ca. 5-10 minutes of performance footage that demonstrates a variety of styles. Please do not submit more than 20 minutes of footage total. Please make sure the video links are set up so anyone can view them.
